question: Should OpenClaw permanently ship the bundled 1Password SecretRef provider that executes a trusted local `op` CLI with a plugin-owned service-account credential, along with the new shared plugin-SDK setup-plan API?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and backed by live proof, but choosing the lasting secret-execution and public SDK boundary is a maintainer product-and-security decision rather than a mechanical contributor follow-up.

options.title: Approve the bounded provider contract
options.body: Accept the opt-in managed provider and shared SDK helper after the changelog edit is removed and the rebased head is rechecked.

options.title: Keep the provider private to this plugin
options.body: Require a narrower internal helper or duplicated local setup logic if maintainers do not want to publish this SDK contract yet.

options.title: Pause bundled support
options.body: Defer the built-in 1Password SecretRef provider if the host-executable trust boundary should remain outside the bundled plugin set.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded provider contract
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in managed provider and shared SDK helper after the changelog edit is removed and the rebased head is rechecked.
